context: Equipment types answer different questions: where is it, what group operates together, what function is maintained, and which physical item is installed? A replacement changes physical identity without necessarily changing the maintained function.
Work history and cost scope depend on the selected equipment record and hierarchy configuration. Design the hierarchy around operational reporting requirements, not only the physical layout.
25.check: A replacement pump should receive its own physical asset identity. Review the existing relationship and history policy before changing the position association.

context: Asset identity is the basis for tracking work, warranty, procurement and history. The archived Help describes ASSETASS for purchase-order recognition and AUTOANUM for automatic numbering. Status values can be configured; do not copy a status list blindly.
Before creating the record, agree whether the equipment is asset-tracked through purchasing. A manual entry can duplicate an asset that will be recognized automatically.
example: Separate functional identity; establish hierarchy separately
31.check: Retrieve PUMP-001 in the list view and inspect its organization, status and intended structure. Where regulatory checklist items are unresolved, consult the documented operational-status restriction.

context: Think of a position as a job that a physical asset performs. A pump can leave that job and a new pump can occupy it. Keep physical serial and purchase history separate from the position's functional context.
36.check: Inspect the hierarchy before and after replacement and confirm the approved cost/history treatment.

context: Define parents before children. The Help explains equipment hierarchy restrictions and links to cost and meter information. A valid hierarchy is not always a simple four-level tree: different relationship types and permitted parents may exist.

For implementation, agree which relationships represent physical containment, functional dependence and intended rollups. Test the behavior rather than assuming every parent receives every child cost.

A physical meter measures usage; its reading may have a physical maximum or reset. A logical meter accumulates usage in the maintenance model. The two concepts help distinguish device readings from total usage.
For usage-driven maintenance, the unit and continuity of the meter are fundamental. Investigate unusual readings before generating due work.
EAM separates the purchase unit, stocking unit, and issue/consumption unit. A missing or inverted conversion factor causes immediate stock valuation and quantity errors during receiving and issuing.
Always test unit conversions with small quantities in a non-production store before activating high-volume parts.
175.check: Receive 1 BOX in test and confirm stock increases by 10 EA at one-tenth the box unit price.

context: A store is the stock-holding context. A bin is an internal location, while the part defines what is stocked. The Help states that PRICETYP supplies the default Price Type at store creation, which may be modified as applicable.

A part code identifies a material item, not a unique installed physical asset. Tracking settings determine whether lot, asset or core information is needed in later transactions. Core-tracked parts can enter repair processes.
Define purchasing and stocking units deliberately. Supplier catalog references and part-store settings are related but separate records.
example: Confirm policy before setting tracking options

context: A part can be held at different stores with different stock settings. Minimum stock and reorder quantities are planning data; on-hand balance is transactional data. The selected price level influences cost information.
Replenishment must consider the configured rules and existing supply or demand. This example is not a vendor replenishment formula.
example: Illustrative gap only, not calculated order quantity

context: A requisition expresses need. The purchase order is a separate purchasing record, and the receipt records goods or service fulfillment. A stock item, direct material and service have different business destinations.
Review the header and lines before approval. A requisition number alone does not prove that an order has been placed.
PO receipts confirm physical arrival of goods or services and link back to specific purchase order lines. Partial receipts keep the line open for the remaining balance.
Install parameters and receiving options determine whether packing slips, inspection holds, or direct-to-work-order issues trigger automatically.
233.check: Confirm stock on-hand increased by 3 and PO line open balance reflects 2 remaining.

context: Issuing parts moves physical stock out of a store/bin into a work order, equipment, or project cost center. Unlike a reservation, an issue reduces on-hand quantity and posts material cost immediately.
242.check: Verify both stock reduction in R5STOCK/R5BINSTOCK and the posted transaction in material history.

context: Store-to-store transfers separate dispatch (issue) from arrival (receipt) so stock in transit between warehouses is tracked accurately rather than disappearing from reporting.
Physical inventory freezes or snapshots expected book quantities on count sheets so discrepancies can be investigated before posting authorized inventory adjustments.
276.check: Never post blind adjustments without checking unposted issues or pending receipts.

context: A purchase order header identifies the supplier, organization and commercial context. Lines describe individual goods or services. Approval limits may constrain the originating user; consult the documented rules for the selected release.
Do not treat a requisition, purchase order and receipt as interchangeable. Use the document references to reconcile quantities through the lifecycle.
299.check: Check line quantity, unit, price, currency, receiving store and authorized status before transmitting a purchase commitment.

context: Invoice vouchers perform three-way matching across Purchase Order price, Receipt quantity, and Supplier Invoice amount before releasing financial settlement.
315.check: Investigate price or quantity tolerances before forcing an invoice voucher approval.

context: Task plans are reusable templates for inspection steps, standard trades, estimated hours, and checklists. Updating a task plan revision controls how future work activities inherit standard procedures without altering historical work orders.
Work request approval acts as a gatekeeper between reported issues and scheduled maintenance execution, checking duplicate requests, budget ownership, and status authorizations.
A work order header answers what, where and why; activities answer how work is divided and what resources are needed. Header status and activity completion are related but not interchangeable.

A work request can be reviewed before release. Status authorization, configured user codes, organization access and required fields can influence the actual path. Never assume a training status sequence is a universal system sequence.
Planned labor and materials are estimates; bookings and issues are actual transactions. Keep them distinct when reviewing costs.
example: Business problem, not a repair diagnosis
367.check: Confirm the record appears in the intended work list and the organization and equipment are correct. If approval is blocked, check status authorizations separately from screen update permission.

context: Multiple activities may belong to one work order. An activity number identifies a task within its parent, so an activity number alone is not a reliable reporting key. The supplied R5ACTIVITIES key export lists ACT_EVENT and ACT_ACT.
Task and job plans may supply reusable planning information. Review the actual activity's work scope, trade, estimated duration and required parts after applying templates.
example: Do not replace estimates with booked hours without policy

context: Labor booking posts actual technician hours against a specific work order activity and employee/trade, generating labor cost transactions subject to BOOKDATE and COMDAYS rules.
Cost reporting requires clarity about scope: one work order, a hierarchy, a project or an organization. Joining labor and material detail directly can multiply values when both have many rows.
The example adds independent cost components once. Actual cost inclusion, rates, currency and rollup depend on configuration and transaction scope.

PM schedule timing and recurring work content are distinct. A meter-driven schedule relies on valid readings; a calendar-driven schedule relies on date and interval settings. The Help also describes generation windows and combined options.
Define the schedule, its activities and the equipment-specific association; verify first due and generation rules before processing. Forecasting is a planning view, not proof that work exists.
example: Simple training example; windows/settings may affect generation

context: A PM schedule can describe a reusable maintenance requirement. Equipment association identifies where the requirement applies and establishes relevant equipment-level timing information. Do not assume all equipment starts with the same reading or due date.

The Generate Work Orders form separates selection criteria from preview. Review eligibility and existing work before processing. Batch operation may affect several records, so test criteria with a small scope first.
Closing a work order finalizes execution history and prevents further ad-hoc cost postings, provided mandatory checklists, open child work orders, and closing codes are satisfied.
PM plans group multiple intervals or schedules (e.g., 30-day inspection and 90-day overhaul) under one coordinated maintenance framework per equipment fleet.
Permit-to-work enforces isolation, hazard review, and multi-role signoff before maintenance begins on high-risk equipment—distinct from merely tagging a permit code on a work order.
Calibration management records as-found and as-left measurements on critical instruments against traceable standards to prove compliance and flag out-of-tolerance drift.
User-defined fields (UDFs) add lightweight custom attributes to supported EAM tables without schema changes, whereas Custom Fields attach dynamically by Equipment/Part Class.
Alert Management runs scheduled SQL grids (via the ALRT job driver) to trigger notifications or follow-up work orders when operational thresholds are breached.

Multi-organization security affects record ownership and visibility. The archived topic describes organization defaulting from the login session and notes that Organization is not shown when MOS is not used. Enabling MOS for an entity can be irreversible; review the actual administration guidance before changes.

Screen access permits users to reach a function; query, insert and update permissions control supported record actions. Status authorization is a distinct decision about allowed transitions. A user who can edit a record may not be allowed to approve it.
709.check: Test the same record with both roles and capture the transition, not just whether the screen opened.

context: Imports and exports transfer structured configuration or master data across environments using validated templates—always test small batches in non-production first.

An approval workflow defines source record status, activation, approval decisions and outcomes. Step conditions and parameters should implement a documented business policy. Test positive and negative paths before activation.
example: Example policy, not a delivered default
Expected ordinary approval path per policy
Confirm boundary definition and extra approval path
